title: Nervous Systems: Quantified Life and the Social Question
editor: Anselm Franke; Stephanie Hankey; Marek Tuszynski

description.main: Catalogue of the 2016 HKW Berlin exhibition on data, sensors and power, edited by Anselm Franke, Stephanie Hankey and Marek Tuszynski. Art, essays and historical documents on how digital infrastructures shape governance and social behaviour.
description.extended:
The catalogue of a 2016 exhibition at Haus der Kulturen der Welt in Berlin, which asks how sensors and data infrastructures bind state, industry and body into systems that register every tremor of power.

The 388-page English-language volume sets contemporary art beside essays, research and historical documents. It examines how big data and digital infrastructure shape governance and social behaviour, and where "the social question" of power and participation surfaces. Contributors include Grégoire Chamayou, Avery F. Gordon, Orit Halpern, Ben Hayes, Tung-Hui Hu, Lawrence Liang, Noortje Marres, Matteo Pasquinelli, Nishant Shah and Mushon Zer-Aviv. Joris and Terry Kritis designed the small, softcover book.

Anselm Franke edited it for HKW with Stephanie Hankey and Marek Tuszynski, who are from the Tactical Technology Collective. Spector Books published it in Leipzig in April 2016. Pasquinelli, who writes here, later published The Eye of the Master.

notes: Spector lists 388 pages; some retailers list 386. Co-published with HKW (Haus der Kulturen der Welt). Exhibition dates differ between HKW (10 Mar to 9 May 2016) and Blackwell's. Only one ISBN found. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
